A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Causally Reliable Concept Bottleneck Models and contain complete main text and Appendices A–G. Text and visual inspection support reliable comparison; appendix pages 23–41 are identical.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification, graph-discovery, intervention, debiasing, and fairness experiments in Section 5, with additional empirical analyses in Appendix G.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain the same discovery pipeline, encoder, separate hypernetworks, structural equations, and training objective. The redrawn Figure 2 illustrates existing components rather than changing the procedure.

E1.justification: The five Bayesian-network datasets, cMNIST, CelebA, CUBC, and Siim-Pneumothorax remain, including the reduced-bottleneck, distribution-shift, and fairness scenarios. Figure 2's different illustrative example does not introduce an evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: The evaluated neural and graph-discovery comparators remain unchanged, including appendix comparisons. Table 2 renames 'CBM' to 'Flat CBM' and '+LLM' to 'CD + LLM'; these denote the same existing comparison rows.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices E–G retain the same sample sizes, splits, preprocessing, metrics, training settings, and intervention procedures. For example, synthetic datasets still use 10,000 samples with 70%/10%/20% splits.

E4.justification: The discovery-method, LLM, and RAG ablations, sample-complexity analysis, graph-corruption and flattening tests, and intervention analyses are unchanged. The debiasing experiment and Appendix D.2 interpretation example are also retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-run reporting for main accuracy and intervention results and three-run reporting for specified appendix ablations, with uncertainty expressed as twice the standard error of the mean.

E6.justification: Main-text and appendix result values and plotted findings are unchanged. Table 2 retains Sachs Hamming distances of 3.4 after CD and 1.8 after refinement; Table 3 retains C2BM's post-intervention CaCE of 0.0 ± 0.0%.

T1.justification: The SCM definitions, probability factorization and training derivation, Appendix D.1 universal-approximation theorem and proof, and Appendix F.1 custom Hamming-distance definition are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about causal reliability, automatic instantiation, maintained accuracy, improved interventions, debiasing, and fairness.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability qualifications are retained, including limitations concerning background-knowledge quality, causal-discovery scalability, and encoder distribution shift. The diagram revision adds no substantive new interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendices B–F retain the same filtering rules, prompt templates, RAG settings, implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and code-access statements. Figure 2's illustrative prompt callouts do not revise the documented experimental prompts.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited works are unchanged, as are the stated relationships to prior concept-based and causal models.

P1.justification: Figure 2's caption explicitly names the pipeline stages and specifies 'forward and interventional' queries; Table 2's terminology is clarified. The substantive prose and section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes a taller, two-tier schematic showing CPDAG learning, graph refinement, and separate hypernetworks. Table 2 expands from a text-wrapped display to full width with clearer labels. Figure 4 and other material shift through pagination; appendix visuals remain identical.

improvement.justification: The revised Figure 2 more explicitly communicates graph construction and parameter generation, while the enlarged Table 2 improves legibility and comparator identification. These provide a limited improvement in exposition; the scientific evidence, theory, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
